text:
IncidentBot: [INCIDENT] Preemptible GPU exhaustion in us-west-2 — autoscaler failed to recover after a preemptible churn, queue spike observed. Paging on-call.

Maya: paging @Ian (oncall) — we’re seeing sustained queue growth on text-gen-prod, throttling at 95% capacity. Customers hitting 503s.

Ian (oncall): got it, looking. what's the current queue length? any failed scale actions?

Drew: queue ~18k waiting, processing rate dropped from ~1.2k/s to 200/s after a wave of preemptions. Autoscaler attempted 6 scale-ups, 4 failed with `Insufficient capacity` and 2 stuck in provisioning.

Elena: confirm preemptible eviction surge ~12 nodes in last 7m, GCE reported `PREEMPTION` events. fallback pool (dedicated-burst) at 70% already.

Ian (oncall): start mitigation plan: 1) pause low-priority batch jobs, 2) open emergency burst to dedicated pool (manual), 3) route critical customers to reduced-rate path if possible.

Jordan: pausing batch queues now: `batch.consumers.pause(low-priority)` executed. Should free ~800 slots.

Maya: support ticket spike incoming — using template: "We are experiencing degraded API throughput due to capacity churn; engineers are mitigating." posting to status page.

SupportBot: created ticket INC-4592 and posted status: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/INC-4592 :rotating_light:

Drew: manual scale request to dedicated pool submitted: `rctl scale dedicated-burst +10 --force` — cloud provider returning `QuotaExceeded` for region us-west-2 on GPU quota.

Ian (oncall): Ugh. Check other regions for available capacity. If us-east-1 has slack, route canary traffic there.

Elena: us-east-1 has ~6 spare nodes but networking egress may add latency. For critical customers we can failover.

Maya: creating a customer impact list. Early signs: 12 enterprise customers > 5% error rate, 40 small apps temporarily throttled.

Jordan: starting graceful degradation rule: send `x-redwood-priority=high` through routing rule to prefer cached KV and smaller models. Implemented via `routing/priority` feature flag.

Drew: autoscaler logs:
```
2026-03-14T15:02:12Z scale attempt id=789 provision request GPUs=12 result=quota_error
2026-03-14T15:05:34Z scale attempt id=790 provision request GPUs=8 result=timeout
```
Looks like API calls to cloud are timing out during eviction window.

IncidentBot: Incident severity raised to Sev2 — customer-facing errors, partial region outage.

Ian (oncall): initiating handoff to @Drew for focused mitigation — I'm moving to coordinate customer comms and exec updates. Drew, take operational lead.

Drew: taking lead. Immediate tasks: 1) open limit increase with cloud support (ticket > urgent), 2) spin up fallbacks in eu-west-1/us-east-1, 3) enforce strict autoscaler cooldowns to avoid thundering.

Elena: cloud support ticket opened: CS-11234. ETA initial response ~20m. Meanwhile starting manual spin in eu-west-1: `rctl provision --region eu-west-1 g4dn.xlarge:6`

Jordan: setting routing fallback for critical customers to eu-west-1. Adding header-based routing `x-redwood-fallback: eu-west-1` to a small test cohort.

Maya: status update posted to customers: "We are routing critical traffic to fallback regions and reducing non-essential workloads. Root cause: preemptible GPU churn combined with limited fallback quota."

Drew: spun 4 nodes in eu-west-1, agents registered but model sync backlog ~22 minutes — warmup required. Starting model warmup using `sync-models --models default-small,default-medium --parallel 6`.

Ian (oncall): handoff note for next on-call: keep monitoring queue and customer error rates. If >10 enterprise customers hit >20% errors escalate to Sev1 and loop in SRE Manager.

Elena: observed autoscaler behavior: during rapid eviction it interpreted transient drop in capacity as signal to scale down older heterogeneous pools. Filed PR to change scale-down TTL to 10m.

Drew: temporary mitigation: set autoscaler min_instances for text-gen-prod to current stable baseline (`min=40`) to prevent immediate downscaling while replenishing.

Maya: support update: enterprise customers A,B,C notified privately. CS reps standing by.

SupportBot: queued follow-ups for customer A,B,C — templates applied.

Jordan: monitoring: error rate trending down from 18% to 7% since routing changes and eu-west warmups. Queue length down to ~6.4k.

Drew: cloud support responded: increased soft quota in us-west-2 by +8 GPUs pending review; estimate 45m. They recommend moving away from heavy reliance on preemptible for critical pools.

Ian (oncall): tagging postmortem owners: Drew (ops), Elena (autoscaler), Jordan (routing), Maya (customer comms). Please start collecting logs: autoscaler, provisioning, cloud preemption events, routing traces.

Maya: logging list compiled at https://internal.redwood.ai/incidents/1768000456/logs — added first-draft customer impact table.

Elena: temporary config applied: `autoscaler.scale_down_ttl=600` and `min_instances=40` — will revert after stabilization.

Drew: confirm last manual action: drained low-priority batches, increased min, spun region fallbacks, warmup started. Next target: ensure model variant fallbacks active (quantized v2).

Ian (oncall): final note before signoff: leaving for dinner, handover complete. Drew you're primary until 18:30Z, then @Jordan takes overnight watch. Keep incidentBot updates every 10m.

Drew: acknowledged. will post hourly summary and a 1-hour status after this message.

IncidentBot: Incident update: severity stable at Sev2, queue decreasing, dedicated fallback active, cloud quota pending.

Jordan: end-of-thread checklist: collect timeline, dump scaler logs, capture model warmup metrics, gather customer impact, and schedule postmortem meeting 24-48h.

Maya: thanks all. postmortem owners please add to calendar invite: `Postmortem: 1768000456 - Preemptible capacity exhaustion` — tentative: 2026-03-15 16:00Z. :white_check_mark:
